spec_match.rationale: Composes the new backing-store spaces with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter' — the addition the linear spaces exist to make physically meaningful — with identical native drawing code on both panels when the store is available.

interactive.rationale: Per-light colour inputs and position range sliders redraw both panels via rAF-throttled handlers; the overlap pixel between lights 1 and 2 is re-sampled and printed after every change.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises movable lights whose overlaps disagree between the two number systems, which is what the panels show and the sampled bytes quantify.

edge_cases.rationale: The rejected-store branch swaps in a JS reference rendering labelled in the banner, on the panel badge, and in the readout; clamping at 1.0 in the additive model is explicit in the reference code.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5122501071994880, the HTML spec colour-spaces section, and siblings.

conformance.rationale: Backed by the feature suite's round-trip and conversion assertions that gate this page's native path; the additive claim itself rests on the same store contract the suite pins. Suite verified executing on /conformance/.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable here): autorun DOM shows overlap bytes gamma [95,86,8] vs linear [156,139,95]; desktop screenshot read — the two panels are visibly different additive results with the amber simulation badge on the lower one; mobile 360 no page overflow; zero page console errors over CDP.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts spotlights-native-linear-store or spotlights-js-reference-fallback on load and spotlights-overlap-sampled per redraw with sampled bytes.

design_system.rationale: Chrome uses styles.css variables; badges pass AA as light-on-accent pairs; range/color inputs get explicit focus-visible outlines; canvas content colours are the demo subject, not UI chrome.

accessibility.rationale: Every input has a visible label ('Light N colour/position'), sliders are native range inputs at 44px height, canvases carry role=img aria-labels, and the overlap readout is an aria-live text equivalent of the visual difference.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Sliders cap at min(240px, 60vw) so rows wrap cleanly; CDP-measured no horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3; both class screenshots read.

openQuestions.title: Verify native additive equality (two half-lights equal one full light) on Chrome 155
openQuestions.detail: On a browser with the native srgb-linear store, add an equality check: two overlapping lights at half linear intensity should sample identically to one full-intensity light at the same spot. That assertion is only meaningful against the native store, so it waits for a 155/flag-enabled runtime.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Avoid main-thread jank from high-frequency input-driven rendering; coalesce work per frame.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Slider input redraws are coalesced through a requestAnimationFrame guard (rafPending) so continuous dragging renders at most once per frame, including the per-pixel JS reference path.

guidanceConsulted.query: range slider accessible label visible focus
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Native range inputs with programmatic and visible labels, plus explicit focus indication.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each slider is a native input[type=range] nested in a visible text label; focus-visible outlines are defined for all inputs.

summary: Novel-composition concept pairing the linear backing store with 'lighter' additive compositing: three movable lights whose overlaps oversaturate under gamma addition and stay photon-proportional under linear addition. Honest labelled JS reference where the native store is rejected. Verified in headless Chromium 141 at both classes with clean console.
